decisions.quote: Here we reexamine Moran et al.’s data using more fine-grained analytic strategies. We show that the contingency awareness measures used by Olson and Fazio and, by extension, Moran et al. lack adequate reliability and validity. Moreover, even assuming valid awareness measures, Bayesian analyses did not provide unambiguous evidence for unaware EC effects under any exclusion criterion and provided decisive evidence against such effects in most models. Finally, a separate analysis that distinguished between fully aware, partially aware, and fully unaware participants shows that evidence for unaware EC is due to the inclusion of partially aware participants in the purportedly unaware subsample.
decisions.reason: The paper proceeds directly to evaluating measurement reliability and conducting alternative Bayesian and subgroup reanalyses of the Moran et al. (2021) dataset rather than auditing whether the original reported numbers could be computationally recovered.
